title: Deployment readiness & observability onboarding - AtriaHealth Systems
summary: Kickoff to align on deployment readiness, observability/tracing, VPC network intake and pilot success metrics. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, K/V cache expectations, and audit/log retention needs. Agreed to a small pilot in staging and a subsequent network intake session.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-04-10 15:00 PST
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Sasha Rivera, Daniel Park, Leah Kim; Priya Malhotra, Ethan Cole, Maya Li, Jordan Price

Summary (auto): Quick orientation to Redwood runtime and staging pilot plan, outline next steps for network access and security docs.

[00:00] Sasha Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sasha, AE on the account. Quick roll call please.
[00:12] Priya Malhotra: Priya here, Director of ML at AtriaHealth.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: Ethan, platform eng.
[00:17] Maya Li: Maya, security.
[00:20] Jordan Price: Jordan - SRE.
[00:22] Daniel Park: Daniel Park, solutions engineer, I'll walk through the runtime/observability bits.
[00:30] Sasha Rivera: Great. Goal for today is to make sure we have an actionable pilot plan: network intake, onboarding runbook, observability dashboard templates, and define success metrics.
[02:05] Daniel Park: I'll start with a short overview of the Redwood serving runtime - high level: continuous batching, KV cache, and routing policies. Sorry, sometimes the transcript puts K V cache as K-V. It's the same thing - key value cache for prefixes.
[03:12] Ethan Cole: On KV cache - curious how stateful that is across restarts, like if we're using Dedicated pools and pods reschedule, do we lose the warm cache?
[04:01] Daniel Park: Good question. For Dedicate - sorry Redwood Dedicated - we typically keep GPUs pinned to a pool; but if you do autoscale and nodes are reaped you'll see cache misses. We have cache warmup strategies and prefix caching to reduce that. We'll share our caching whitepaper.
[05:48] Maya Li: Security: what about log retention and PII controls? We need SOC2-like audit trails, and ability to forward audit logs to our SIEM.
[06:20] Leah Kim: We can push audit logs and access traces to your S3 or a syslog endpoint; also we support KMS integrations for customer-managed keys in Private deployments. For hosted, there is envelope encryption and limited retention by default, but we can extend retention under enterprise plans.
[07:35] Priya Malhotra: We expect to keep logs for 1 year and have redaction at rest for patient identifiers. Is that something Redwood can handle?
[08:12] Daniel Park: Yes, redaction is doable in the pipeline, but usually customers do an ingest step to scrub PHI before sending. For Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) you get more control. We'll connect you to our compliance doc pack.
[09:40] Jordan Price: Network question - we use transit-gateway peering and internal-only RDS. How do we do the network intake for a staging pilot?
[10:10] Sasha Rivera: We'll need your network diagram, CIDR ranges, and firewall egress rules; our infra team will do a one-off review. Action: schedule a network intake working session.
[11:23] Ethan Cole: Latency targets: in prod we need 99p latency < 200ms for short queries and throughput ~200 reqs/sec for embeddings batch jobs. Any suggestions?
[12:03] Daniel Park: For sub-200ms you probably want Dedicated with local region routing and a smaller batch size. There's tradeoffs with cost. We can do a short benchmark in staging with a trimmed prompt set to validate tail latency.
[13:40] Priya Malhotra: Let's define pilot success: 1) perf within 20% of our latency baseline, 2) cost estimate per 1M tokens, 3) end-to-end tracing in our observability stack.
[14:02] Leah Kim: I'll capture that as the success criteria.
[15:30] Daniel Park: Observability — we ship per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. For APM/Tracing you can integrate spans into Datadog/NewRelic; we also provide a hosted traces UI in Redwood Console.
[16:18] Maya Li: On tracing, do you propagate request IDs and user identifiers so we can correlate? Need to ensure the IDs are pseudonymized.
[16:40] Daniel Park: We propagate a request_id header; you can also pass an external user id but we recommend pseudonymization. We'll include our header spec in the docs.
[18:05] Priya Malhotra: Can we see a pre-built dashboard for token cost vs latency per route?
[18:20] Leah Kim: Yes - we have dashboard templates. We'll drop a staging Grafana and a console dashboard example.
[19:55] Jordan Price: For the staging pilot, what's the recommended isolation? Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted? We're leaning Private because of data residency but want minimal ops overhead.
[20:30] Daniel Park: Private gives you the best control but needs more setup (VPC, routing). Dedicated is middle ground - reserved GPU pools but still managed. Hosted is fastest to start. For regulatory workloads, customers often choose Private or Dedicated with strict VPC peering and KMS.
[22:01] Ethan Cole: Any estimates for setup time? We have a Q3 launch window.
[22:20] Sasha Rivera: Typical Private onboarding is ~6-8 weeks, Dedicated is ~3-4 weeks, Hosted pilot can be live in days. For Q3 we can scope a Dedicated pilot in May-June to hit ramp.
[23:55] Priya Malhotra: Ok we need to lock down timeline, who's the primary contact?
[24:10] Sasha Rivera: Leah Kim (CSM) will be your onboarding lead. I'll coordinate contractual stuff. Daniel will handle tech runbooks and benchmarks.
[25:40] Daniel Park: Quick tech note: for embeddings batch jobs we recommend async routes with batching window tuned; for low-latency chat we recommend dynamic batching off for critical paths.
[26:45] Maya Li: Regarding KMS - you mentioned HSM support? We need to know if we can use our enterprise HSM.
[27:10] Daniel Park: We integrate with major cloud KMS providers; for on-prem HSM we offer private deployment options that can hook to your HSM via a connector. I'll flag our security eng to follow up.
[28:52] Ethan Cole: How do we measure token-level cost in the console? Do you break out generation vs prompt tokens?
[29:12] Leah Kim: Yes, token-level breakdown is available; we can also give per-route cost and per-model cost charts. We'll send a sample cost-export CSV from an existing pilot.
[30:50] Priya Malhotra: Any competitors we should be aware of from your side who do similar setups?
[31:05] Sasha Rivera: Some customers evaluate MegaCloud AI and InferStack for Hosted endpoints; for self-hosted runtimes, teams look at OpenServe. We'll send a short competitor comparison.
[32:30] Jordan Price: Questions about failover - if a model variant becomes unresponsive, does Redwood auto-fall back?
[32:55] Daniel Park: Yes, we support routing policies with automatic fallback to compatible model variants and region failover. You can also set per-route fallback policies in the console.
[34:20] Ethan Cole: Let's talk data flow: do we persist prompts on Redwood side by default?
[34:40] Leah Kim: By default we store logs for 30 days for hosted; for Dedicated/Private you can define retention or disable persistence. We'll document the exact retention knobs.
[36:01] Priya Malhotra: Action: we need the security/compliance pack + network intake template.
[36:15] Sasha Rivera: On it.
[38:00] Daniel Park: I'll also prepare a staging benchmark plan: sample prompts, load shape, and scripts.
[39:10] Priya Malhotra: Are there any known limitations with sequence length or quantized models we should watch for?
[39:30] Daniel Park: Long sequence lengths can increase latency, obviously. For quantized models we recommend the quantization profiles we maintain; some older hardware may have different kernel behaviors - we'll include recommended model+quantization pairings.
[41:05] Maya Li: On auditability, can we get an exportable audit trail showing who invoked which route and when?
[41:26] Leah Kim: Yes, we provide audit logs that can be exported and shipped to your SIEM. We'll share a sample log format.
[43:00] Jordan Price: Network intake scheduling - who will own that from Atria side?
[43:12] Ethan Cole: I'll own the network intake and provide diagrams and CIDRs by Friday.
[43:25] Priya Malhotra: I'll be the exec sponsor and will expect weekly syncs during the pilot.
[44:02] Sasha Rivera: Great. Any other blockers?
[44:20] Priya Malhotra: Need SSO and RBAC details; we use SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[44:45] Leah Kim: We support SAML and SCIM; we'll provide a SSO integration guide.
[46:10] Daniel Park: Final technical note: we'll run a small loadtest in staging to validate 99p latency and will share raw metrics.
[47:05] Jordan Price: Do you have a runbook for incident response?
[47:20] Leah Kim: Yes, we'll include an incident runbook and contact matrix.
[48:50] Sasha Rivera: Recap - network intake (Ethan), security pack and SSO guide (Leah), staging benchmark plan (Daniel), pilot success criteria agreed.
[50:05] Priya Malhotra: Thanks. Let's get the network docs in by Friday and schedule network intake next week.
[51:12] Leah Kim: I'll send calendar invites and upload docs to the shared folder.
[52:00] Daniel Park: I'll attach sample load scripts and caching whitepaper.
[53:30] Sasha Rivera: Any closing thoughts?
[53:50] Maya Li: None from me. This was productive.
[54:10] Ethan Cole: Thanks all.
[54:30] Priya Malhotra: Thanks, bye.

(Automated transcript note: occasional word swaps and punctuation may be incorrect.)
